items.title: Define the canonical Proof-or-Stop domain language
items.context: Create a root CONTEXT.md containing only stable domain concepts and precise distinctions such as Claim, Obligation, Evidence, Receipt, Admissibility, Gate, Story, ReviewRun, Finding, Freshness, Material, and Completion Certificate.
items.userSees: A concise canonical glossary distinguishes Proof-or-Stop claims, evidence, receipts, admissibility, gates, findings, freshness, and completion without depending on TypeScript file names.
excludes: Implementation algorithms or TypeScript module paths in CONTEXT.md

happy.desc: A structural verifier confirms the glossary defines every required canonical term as a definition rather than merely naming headings.

edge.desc: The verifier confirms the glossary explicitly distinguishes Evidence Candidate from admissible Evidence and Task Completion from Production Completion.

adversarial.desc: The verifier rejects missing canonical definitions and rejected aliases, preventing a heading-only glossary from satisfying acceptance.

items.title: Specify the complete evidence-gated lifecycle for an equivalent framework
items.context: Write a requirements document covering philosophy, formal claim and evidence model, lifecycle state machine, per-phase artifact and field contracts, writers and consumers, freshness and signature domains, review and remediation loops, TEST and DONE closure, security boundaries, extension points, migration guidance, and an implementation-neutral acceptance checklist; register it in NAV.
items.userSees: A new-framework team can follow one normative specification from domain model through INIT, INIT_CHECK, PLAN, DEV, REVIEW, TEST, and DONE, including every core artifact field, writer, consumer, invalidation rule, and conformance test.
excludes: Requiring the new framework to use TypeScript, JSON files, Git worktrees, or the current command names
Treating legacy compatibility artifacts as essential semantics
Claiming Proof-or-Stop proves arbitrary functional correctness

happy.desc: The structural verifier confirms the specification covers the complete INIT through DONE state machine and normative entry, exit, rollback, actor, and gate contracts for every phase.

edge.desc: The verifier confirms each lifecycle phase has an artifact table covering requiredness, writer authority, fields, consumers, freshness, and invalidation semantics.

adversarial.desc: The verifier confirms fail-closed typed holes, subject and environment binding, independent review, candidate-versus-completion separation, and a substantive reimplementation conformance checklist are present.
